title: Scalar Ext external cup agrees with the ordinary module cup of pullbacks
statement: Let k be a field [def-weil-field], f:X -> Spec k and g:Y -> Spec k be schemes [def-pc-scheme], F on X and G on Y arbitrary module sheaves, and p,q natural numbers. For any ordinary module cup product cup of pr1^*F and pr2^*G characterized by IsModuleCupProduct [def-sc-module-cohomology-cup-product], and x in scalarCohomology(f,F,p), y in scalarCohomology(g,G,q) [def-sc-field-linear-module-cohomology-operations], externalCup(f,g,F,G,p,q,x,y), on its underlying module-cohomology carrier, equals (-1)^(p*q) times cup(moduleCohomologyPullback(pr1,F,p,x), moduleCohomologyPullback(pr2,G,q,y)) [def-weil-pbc-module-cohomology-fmap]. No Cech cover, comparison, cochain, or total cycle is assumed.

proof.text: Unfold externalCup. Apply the signed scalarCup_moduleCup_compatibility on the fiber product to the two scalar pullbacks, retaining the unchanged resolution characterization hypothesis. Use scalar_moduleCohomologyPullback_comparison for both projections (rfl for the first, pullback.condition.symm for the second). Apply equality congruence to cup and then under multiplication by (-1)^(p*q), and compose the equalities.

theorem scalarExternalCup_moduleComparison
    {k : Type w} [Field k] {X Y : Scheme.{w}}
    (f : X ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k)) (g : Y ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of k))
    (F : X.Modules) (G : Y.Modules) (p q : ℕ)
    (cup : (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology (Limits.pullback f g).toRingedSpace p).obj
        ((tensorPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F) →ₗ[Γ(Limits.pullback f g, ⊤)]
      (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology (Limits.pullback f g).toRingedSpace q).obj
        ((tensorPullback (pullback.snd f g)).obj G) →ₗ[Γ(Limits.pullback f g, ⊤)]
      (RingedSpace.moduleCohomology (Limits.pullback f g).toRingedSpace (p + q)).obj
        (externalCupCoefficients f g F G))
    (hcup :
      ∀ (D : CupResolutionPairing
            ((tensorPullback (pullback.fst f g)).obj F)
            ((tensorPullback (pullback.snd f g)).obj G))
        (a : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor
          (Limits.pullback f g).toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
          D.left.K).sc p).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (b : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor
          (Limits.pullback f g).toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
          D.right.K).sc q).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K)
        (c : ((((RingedSpace.globalSectionsFunctor
          (Limits.pullback f g).toRingedSpace).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℕ)).obj
          D.target.K).sc (p + q)).moduleCatLeftHomologyData.K),
        c.val = D.pair p q ⊤ a.val b.val →
          cup (D.left.class p a) (D.right.class q b) = D.target.class (p + q) c)
    (x : scalarCohomology f F p) (y : scalarCohomology g G q) :
    externalCup f g F G p q x y =
      (-1 : ℤ) ^ (p * q) •
        cup (moduleCohomologyPullback (pullback.fst f g) F p x)
          (moduleCohomologyPullback (pullback.snd f g) G q y)

statement_change.what: The old unsigned normalization omits the Koszul factor. scalarExtCup composes the left class first, so extracting the left shift before the right shift on the (p,q) tensor summand contributes (-1)^(p*q). The prior module's private scalarCup_yoneda_order and oddShiftTensor_component proofs verify the order and the (1,1) sign; oddTensorSummand_ne_neg and oddShiftTensor_not_unsigned show that the sign is nontrivial over the rationals. With the resolution and front/back Cech pairings kept unsigned, the scalar cup is (-1)^(p*q) times their class. Equivalently, the Cech-to-scalar comparison has (-1)^(i.val.1*i.val.2) multiplying its left-hand side. This is a normalization correction, with no new hypotheses; p=0 or q=0, even p*q, characteristic two, and zero classes reduce to the prior formula.
